market_summary:
Singapore banks are the dominant story this week: UOB's Q3 net profit missed consensus and fell 15% QoQ on a trading-income slump, OCBC and DBS have already slid 12-9% over the past month into their own earnings (Nov 5-6), with analysts bracing for rate-compression margin pressure despite record fee income. In the US, Apple beat on revenue but spooked investors with weak December-quarter margin guidance tied to memory costs and AI capex, while Meta's well-subscribed but wider-spread $15bn AI bond deal underscores growing investor wariness of Big Tech's AI debt load. Growth/AI-adjacent names (NVDA, GOOGL, META) remain in pullback mode from 52-week highs, while defensive, low-beta Berkshire Hathaway is bucking the trend with a steady grind higher into its own Nov 7 print. Overall tone is cautious-to-negative on rate-sensitive financials and high-multiple tech, with idiosyncratic strength in quality defensives.</market_summary>
